## Discovery Report: minerva

**1. Documentation found**
- `README.md` — "The Pantheon's Planner." Minerva turns an idea into an approved, planned spec autonomously/headlessly, running the front half of the hive flow (kickoff+plan) via a JSON-over-stdio subprocess ABI. No daemon; state on filesystem under `~/.minerva/runs`.
- `VISION.md` — status v0.1.1, "working (wip)". 3 rungs: ① current (subprocess ABI + drivers work end-to-end), ② near-term (headless pre-baked defaults, land ForkedHiveDriver, wire decision surface, emit planning metrics), ③ long-term (methodology auto-detect, plan-quality metrics, plan A/B, many-ideas-in-parallel self-tuning).
- `docs/architecture.md` — full API contract referenced by dispatch.ts.
- `docs/initial-info.md` — discovery_brief source (already referenced in profile).
- `docs/north-star.md`, `docs/prd.md`, `docs/product-brief.md` — planning docs.
- `docs/minerva-next-tests-and-driver-paths.md`, `docs/scope/forked-driver-integration-next-phase.md`, `docs/spike-plugin-hive-drivability-findings.md` (+ a spike test) — ForkedHiveDriver R&D trail.
- `docs/decisions/kickoff-review.md` — a decision record.
- `docs/ideation/pan-6963/`, `docs/ideation/pan-6965/` — real ideation-loop artifacts (ingested-context, design-discussion, prd, wireframe.html, questions.json, flow.mmd) — evidence the `ideate-to-consus` loop (bin/ideate-to-consus.mjs) has been dogfooded on real tickets.
- `docs/plan-defaults.example.yaml` — example config for pre-baked plan defaults.

**2. Tech stack**
- Language: TypeScript, `type: module`, Node `>=20.19`.
- `tsconfig.json`: ES2022 target, NodeNext module/resolution, `strict: true`, `noUncheckedIndexedAccess: true`, noEmit (tsx runs TS directly, no build step).
- Dependencies: `yaml@^2.9.0` (only runtime dep).
- Dev dependencies: `@types/node`, `tsx@^4.23.1`, `typescript@^5.7.0`.
- Test runner: Node's built-in `node:test` (via `tsx --test`), not Jest/Vitest.
- Scripts: `test` (`tsx --test --test-force-exit --test-concurrency=1` over `src/**/*.test.ts` + `bin/**/*.test.ts`), `typecheck` (`tsc --noEmit`), `ci` (test + typecheck — **local CI only, matches README's "no GitHub Actions" claim for the app-level gate**, though a generic reusable `ci.yml` was added at the repo level, see §6).
- Package manager: npm (`package-lock.json` present, no yarn/pnpm lock).

**3. Project structure**
- `bin/minerva.ts` — the ABI entry point: reads one JSON request from stdin, dispatches, writes response, exit 0/1.
- `bin/minerva-plan.ts` — Auriga-invokable direct plan entry point.
- `bin/ideate-to-consus.mjs` — the ideation loop (idea → questions+wireframe+PRD → Consus), with `--scan` autopilot/auto-resume support.
- `bin/minerva.test.ts` — ABI-level test.
- `src/dispatch.ts` — method registry (`capabilities`, `startRun`, `getRunStatus`, `listRuns`, `getQuestions`, `submitAnswers`, `getOutput`, `abortRun`) → `{result}`/`{error}` envelope.
- `src/kickoff-engine.ts` + `.test.ts` — drives plugin-hive's `kickoff`+`plan` skills headlessly.
- `src/plan-runner.ts` + `.test.ts` — runs the PLAN driver, files decomposed stories into the seed's target project, carries `depends_on`.
- `src/agnostic-plan-driver.ts` — the newest piece (per git log, "runner-agnostic PLAN driver with Heimdall route + bulletproof claude fallback").
- `src/driver.ts` — the swappable `Driver` abstraction: `SpawnDriver` (default, `claude -p`/`--resume`, real SIGINT/SIGTERM hardening via async `spawn()`), `SubagentDriver` (`claude --bg` + poll + stop + resume, orphan-resistant), `ForkedHiveDriver` (intentional stub, throws until plugin-hive-fork exists).
- `src/run-manager.ts` — per-run isolated git workspace management (`~/.minerva/runs`), `getRunStatus`/`listRuns`.
- `src/repo-resolution.ts` + `src/target-repo-signal.ts` — resolve/stamp the real target repo per seed (worktree from `dev` branch, or fresh `git init` for greenfield).
- `src/envelope-detection.ts` — read-only detection of `.pHive/questions/*.yaml` structured envelopes.
- `src/escalation-classification.ts` — classifies extracted questions `agent` vs `human` channel.
- `src/question-extraction.ts` — pulls a turn's question via constrained `--json-schema` call.
- `src/completeness.ts` (implied by test) / `src/deadline-renewal-ownership` — governance around when a run is "done enough."
- `src/output-emitter.ts` — emits approved epic/stories, detects flat + multi-epic plugin-hive layout to auto-fire filing.
- `src/cleanup-ledger.ts` — append-only ledger for external GC; Minerva itself never deletes a workspace.
- `src/plan-defaults.ts` / `src/prebaked-plan-defaults.test.ts` — pre-baked default answers so headless plan runs don't hang.
- `src/capabilities.ts`, `src/errors.ts`, `src/types.test.ts` — shared contract/error types.
- `src/test-cli.ts` — shared test harness helper (`call()`) used across many `*.test.ts` files.
- `src/driver-sigint-harness.ts`, `src/subagent-driver-sigkill-harness.ts` — standalone harness scripts for empirically proving signal-handling behavior (referenced in `driver.ts` comments as real, twice-confirmed findings).

**4. Architecture**
- **Dispatch pattern**: `dispatch.ts` is a flat method-registry dispatcher — `Record<string, Handler>` mapping method name to async handler, wrapping every call in try/catch, normalizing thrown `MinervaError` into `{error: {code, message, retry_after_ms}}`. No DI framework; plain function imports wired directly into the registry.
- **Driver abstraction**: `Driver` interface = single method `runTurn(input) -> {session_id, raw_result}`. Selected via `MINERVA_DRIVER` env var (fails loudly on invalid config, not silently — an explicit repo-wide discipline, e.g. `resolveTurnTimeoutMs()` throws on invalid `MINERVA_TURN_TIMEOUT_MS` rather than falling back silently). Concrete drivers (`SpawnDriver`, `SubagentDriver`, stub `ForkedHiveDriver`) are all validated against one shared contract test in `src/types.test.ts`.
- **Error handling style**: typed `MinervaError` with `ErrorCode` union, explicit fail-loud on misconfiguration (never silently guesses a default for something safety-relevant), heavy inline comments documenting *empirically confirmed* production findings (e.g., execFileSync swallowing SIGINT, `--bg --resume` returning a new session_id) — comments read like incident/spike notes baked into the code.
- **No daemon**: every dispatch is a fresh process; state persists purely on the filesystem (`~/.minerva/runs`), no DB, no server/port.
- **Signal hardening**: module-level single in-flight child tracking + `process.on("SIGINT"/"SIGTERM")` handlers that kill the child and exit with the correct POSIX-shifted code (130/143).

**5. Test infrastructure**
- 22 `*.test.ts` files (21 non-test `.ts` source files) — essentially 1:1 test-to-source ratio, co-located (no separate `__tests__/`).
- Runner: Node's native `node:test` module (`import { test, before, after } from "node:test"`), executed via `tsx --test`, forced single-concurrency (`--test-concurrency=1`) and forced exit (`--test-force-exit`) — likely because tests spawn real subprocesses/child processes.
- No coverage tool configured (no istanbul/c8/nyc in package.json).
- `src/test-cli.ts` provides a shared `call()` test helper used across most `*.test.ts` files — a lightweight in-house test-CLI harness rather than a mocking framework.
- No mocking library present (no jest.mock/mockk equivalent) — tests appear to exercise real subprocess/filesystem behavior directly (consistent with the driver harness files and "empirically confirmed" comment style).

**6. CI/CD**
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` — generic, reusable Pantheon-wide gate: auto-detects stack (node/python/go) via marker files, runs install+build+test on PRs into `dev`/`main`/`master` plus `workflow_dispatch`. For Node it runs `npm ci`, `npm run build --if-present`, then `npm test` if a test script exists. This is a shared/templated workflow, not Minerva-specific.
- `.github/workflows/promote.yml` — on push to `dev`, opens (or reuses, idempotently) a `dev -> default-branch` PR; does NOT enable auto-merge (deliberately, so `GITHUB_TOKEN` can't bypass the CI gate on bot-opened PRs); actual merge is handled by "the existing review squad."
- Note: README's closing line says "local CI, no GitHub Actions" — that refers to Minerva's own `npm run ci` script being the authoritative gate; the `.github/workflows/` present are Pantheon's standard cross-repo CI/promote scaffolding (added in a later commit `ci: add standard CI/CD workflows`), not a contradiction but two layers.

**7. Conventions**
- Commit style: Conventional-Commits-flavored (`feat(scope): ...`, `fix(scope): ...`, `docs: ...`, `ci: ...`), several referencing Linear ticket IDs (`PAN-6745`, `pan-6965`) and epic/story bracket tags (`[wire-forked-driver-selection]`, `[deadline-renewal-ownership]`).
- Branch naming: `feat/<slug-or-ticket>` (e.g. `feat/PAN-8562`, `feat/prebaked-plan-defaults`), plus generated `run/<uuid>` branches (Minerva's own per-run workspaces pushed to origin) and `recovered/<sha>` — the `run/*` and UUID-named `feat/*` branches are almost certainly Minerva's own dogfooded output, not human-authored.
- `main` and `dev` both exist as long-lived branches; `promote.yml` implies `dev -> main` is the real merge flow, though local `git branch` shows checked out on `main` directly.
- File naming: kebab-case `.ts` files, `*.test.ts` co-located, `*-harness.ts` suffix for standalone empirical-proof scripts.

**8. Integration preflight**
- `codex`: detected at `/Users/mdostal/.local/bin/codex` (profile listed path as `/Users/dostal/...` — stale/wrong username, should be corrected to `/Users/mdostal/.local/bin/codex`).
- `multica`: detected, but path differs from profile — now at `/opt/homebrew/bin/multica`, profile says `/Users/dostal/.local/bin/multica` (also stale username AND stale path — likely reinstalled via brew since last kickoff).
- `linearis`, `frame0`, `maestro`: still not found on PATH — matches profile's `detected: false`.
- MCP servers: this session has a `posthog` MCP server connected (per this session's system instructions) — not previously reflected in the profile's `integrations.mcp_servers` block (which lists posthog as `detected: false`). Worth flagging for correction, though this is session-level MCP config, not necessarily project-level.

**9. Code quality tooling**
- No `.eslintrc*`, no `eslint.config.*`, no Prettier config, no `.husky/`, no `lefthook.yml`/`.lefthook.yml`, no `.pre-commit-config.yaml` found anywhere in the repo root. Zero linter/formatter/pre-commit tooling configured — relies solely on `tsc --strict` + the TDD test suite as the quality gate (`npm run ci` = test + typecheck).

**10. Project maturity signal**
- **Actively growing, not early-prototype.** Real evidence: ~7,000 lines across 43 TS files with near-1:1 test coverage, a versioned release (`0.1.1`), a documented and working subprocess ABI with 8 real methods, two working Driver implementations plus one honest stub, empirically-validated signal-handling hardening (harness scripts proving real production bugs), a CI/promote pipeline, and dogfooded ideation artifacts on real tickets (`docs/ideation/pan-6963`, `pan-6965`). Not yet "mature/stable" — VISION.md explicitly self-describes as "working (wip)," `ForkedHiveDriver` is an intentional stub, and there's no lint/format tooling or coverage measurement yet. Best characterized as **actively-growing / pre-1.0 real system**, not a prototype.

Out of scope note: profile correction of the two stale integration paths (codex/multica usernames and multica's new brew path) is a one-line data-freshness fix the parent may want to apply directly rather than re-running discovery.
